active_family: 612a native joint38 AR transition with conditional source scale
current_bottleneck: Naive learned source scale is degenerate under plain flow matching: the source-scale head collapsed to the lower clamp 0.25 after epoch 2, so the sharply better validation loss did not represent learned state-responsive risk width. The full suite improved to 6/11, but regime layer2 remained 0/8, persistent severe undercoverage stayed 9.3%, turbulent/calm width was 0.910, h1 mean reversion weakened, and pathwise max-jump KS failed at 0.638.
last_result_summary: 612a added a generic conditional source-scale head to the 609/610 native joint AR transition-flow model and trained joint38 for 8 epochs on 2048 recent windows. The best validation loss dropped to 0.109902, but training diagnostics showed source_scale_mean/std = 0.25/0.0 from epoch 2 onward. Official 441-window/48-sample IV bridge score improved from 610a 5/11 to 6/11: passed surface, conditionality, time_series, block-AR, cointegration, cross-cell correlation; failed coverage, regime_coverage, distributional_fidelity, mean_reversion, pathwise_jump_realism. Key metrics: cov90 77.4%, conditional MAE reduction 11.6%, turb/calm width 0.910, daily KS 24/25, level KS 13/25, median-bias cells 18/25, persistent severe undercoverage 1026/11025 = 9.3%, mean-reversion ratio 0.600, pathwise max-jump KS 0.638.
next_step_recommendation: Close naive trainable source scale as a width mechanism. The next clean experiment should use the existing prefix_feature_mode=scale route: keep one shared joint AR transition model and a fixed source distribution, but expose generic volatility/magnitude features (abs(delta), delta^2) to the causal memory so regime-sensitive transition geometry can be learned without separate IV/factor paths or post-hoc calibration.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 510a, 596a, and 610a all score 5/11. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 610a is the cleanest native joint learned law so far because it generates IV and anchor factors through one shared AR transition model.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
